judge_input.description:
# Summary of Changes

This change deprecates `falcon.testing.redirected`, doing so in favor of the standard library's own `contextlib.redirect_stdout` together with `contextlib.redirect_stderr`.

**Changes:**
- Added a deprecation warning onto `falcon.testing.redirected`, and did this specifically by making use of the `falcon.util.deprecated` helper
- Updated the internal test file (namely the one called `test_cmd_inspect_app.py`) so that it now goes ahead and uses the `contextlib` alternatives instead of what it used before
- This has been scheduled in such a way that the eventual removal will end up happening in Falcon 5.0

**Rationale:**
- The popular pytest framework already goes ahead and captures, and then also suppresses, the output that comes out of the successful tests, and it does this automatically by default without needing to be told
- The stdlib itself already provides the equivalent functionality, doing so by way of both `contextlib.redirect_stdout` and also `contextlib.redirect_stderr`
- It reduces the ongoing maintenance burden that we carry, and it does that by going and removing a utility that had by this point become redundant

# Related Issues

Fixes #2569

# Pull Request Checklist

This is really just a friendly reminder about the most common mistakes that people tend to make. Please do make sure that you go and tick every one of the *appropriate* boxes. Reading through our [contribution guide](https://falcon.readthedocs.io/en/stable/community/contributing.html) at least a single time is something that will end up saving you a good few review cycles down the line!

If it turns out that an item does not actually apply to your particular pull request, then please go ahead and **check it anyway**, since doing that makes it plainly apparent that there is genuinely nothing that needs to be done there.

- [x] Applied the changes to both the WSGI and the ASGI code paths and interfaces (in the places where that is applicable).
- [x] Added **tests** that cover the code which was changed.
- [x] Performed the automated tests along with the code quality checks by way of [running `tox`](https://falcon.readthedocs.io/en/stable/community/contributing.html#pull-requests).
- [x] Prefixed the code comments with a GitHub nick together with an appropriate prefix.
- [x] The coding style is kept consistent with that of the rest of the framework.
- [x] Updated the **documentation** so that it covers the changed code.
    - [x] Added docstrings for any and all new classes, functions, or modules.
    - [x] Updated the docstrings for any modifications made to the existing code.
    - [x] Updated both the WSGI docs and the ASGI docs (wherever that is applicable).
    - [x] Added references pointing to the new classes, functions, or modules over into the relevant RST file that lives under `docs/`.
    - [x] Updated every one of the relevant supporting documentation files that are kept under `docs/`.
    - [x] A copyright notice has been included right at the top of any of the new modules (using either your own name or else the name of your organization).
    - [x] The changed or added classes, methods, and functions all have the appropriate `versionadded`, `versionchanged`, or `deprecated` [directives](http://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/stable/usage/restructuredtext/directives.html?highlight=versionadded#directive-versionadded).
- [x] The changes (along with any possible deprecations) have [towncrier news fragments](https://falcon.readthedocs.io/en/stable/community/contributing.html#changelog) placed under `docs/_newsfragments/`, with the file name given in the format `{issue_number}.{fragment_type}.rst`. (Run `tox -e towncrier`, and then inspect `docs/_build/html/changes/` over in the browser so as to make sure that it renders correctly.)
- [x] Any LLM output, if there happens to be any at all, has been carefully reviewed and then tested by a human developer. (See also: [Use of LLMs ("AI")](https://falcon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/community/contributing.html#use-of-llms-ai).)

If you happen to have *any* questions at all about *any* of the points that are listed above, then just go ahead and **submit and ask**! This whole checklist is here in order to *help* you along, and certainly not to deter you in any way from contributing!

*PR template inspired by the attrs project.*
